bc_squatter_s_bluff_2.blurb: Squatter's Bluff is a small cliff band within Nelson in the West Kootenay region, set uphill from a road junction. It holds seven short routes: six bolted lines and one top-rope, spanning easy 5.6 through to low 5.11. Most of the routes sit at moderate grades. The tallest face stays shaded through hot afternoons, which helps in summer. The bluff sits higher and deeper in the trees than the lower Golf Ball walls beside it, and most lines can be top-roped by walking around the left side to the anchors.

bc_gomer_wall.blurb: Gomer Wall is a yellow-toned cliff inside John's Family Nature Conservancy Regional Park in the Okanagan, near Kelowna. It has seven sport routes, with one around 5.7 and the rest clustered between 5.9 and 5.10. A couple of the longer routes run to two or three pitches. A ledge sits partway up the face, and a stick clip can come in handy. Newer leaders may find the climbing a bit intimidating despite the moderate numbers. Reach it by following the main trail from the lot, then cutting west along the cliff band below the walls.

bc_lonely_pine.blurb: Lonely Pine is a compact sport crag in the Lonely Crags group near Kelowna, up Chute Lake Road, about five minutes' walk beyond Lonely Girl. Its seven bolted routes are short but the rock is good quality, with the bulk of them in the 5.10 to 5.11 range and a single easier line near 5.8, so it suits climbers working at that level. A few routes can also be top-roped. The cliff gets shade in the morning and sun in the afternoon, and the surrounding hillside was cleared by fire, so there is little tree cover.

bc_hall_of_thieves.blurb: Hall of Thieves is a short sport wall in the Lonely Crags area near Kelowna, with lake views nearby. Seven routes are here, mostly well-bolted lines from 5.6 to 5.8, plus a single 5.11, and one can be top-roped. That mix makes it a good spot to build confidence, and new leaders are encouraged to come. There is no tree cover, so the wall bakes in the sun from early afternoon until dusk. The ground at the base is uneven and overgrown, so watch your footing. The anchors give nice views, and the walk in from the lot is short.

bc_the_grotto.blurb: The Grotto is a small bolted crag in the Crumpit Woods near Squamish, reached off the Mamquam forest road. Seven sport routes run from 5.7 up to 5.10d, with two at the easy end, one at 5.9 and the other four in the 5.10 range, so it targets climbers who sit around 5.10 and want something away from the big Squamish classics. Rock quality is described as moderate, with several lines earning three stars. The setting is wooded: the trail crosses a marsh that can be wet, then squeezes through a low, mossy opening into the grotto itself.
